parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Experiment 1
Use a measuring cylinder to pour 25 cm of distilled water into the polystyrene cup provided.
Support the polystyrene cup in the 250 cm beaker. Measure the initial temperature of the
water and record it in the table below.
Add all of solid H to the water in the cup and stir the mixture with the thermometer.
Measure the temperature of the liquid mixture after 90 seconds. Record your result in the table.
Remove the thermometer and rinse the thermometer and the cup with water.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Experiment 2
Repeat Experiment 1, using solid J instead of solid H.
Measure and record the initial and final temperatures in the table below.
Keep some of this solution in a test-tube for Experiment 5.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Experiment 3
Repeat Experiment 1, using solid K. Record the temperatures in the table.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Experiment 4
Repeat Experiment 1 using solid L. Record the temperatures in the table and complete the
table. Keep this solution for Experiment 5.

text: You are going to investigate the addition of four different solids, H, J, K and L, to water.
The same mass of solid, 4 g, will be used in each experiment.
Read all the instructions below carefully before starting the experiments.
You are going to carry out five experiments.

Experiment 5
Pour about 3 cm of the solution from Experiment 2 into a test-tube. Use a teat pipette to add
about 3 cm of the solution from Experiment 4 to the test-tube. Record your observations.
